get.summary: Gets a single article by guid
get.description: Retrieves a single article by its unique identifier.

patch.summary: Updates part of an existing article
patch.description: Updates only article fields included in the request body. Use the partitions endpoint to change the partitions of the article.

delete.description: Deletes the specified article from the system.

get.summary: Gets a single article by barcode
get.description: Retrieves a single article by barcode and barcode type using the {barcode}:{type} route value.

get.summary: Gets a article inventory by guid
get.description: Retrieves the inventory count for an article. When 'at' is supplied, the count is reconstructed from the item containment history as it was at that instant.
Retrieves a paginated list of articles, including the total number of matching entries.

post.description: Creates a new article with optional partitions, barcodes, and active state. Returns the generated identifier.

put.summary: Changes the partitions of an article
put.description: Adds and removes the partitions the an article belongs to in one request. At least one partition is required and none may be in both lists. The caller needs access to every partition it touches. Requires the ChangeArticlePartitions permission.

get.description: Retrieves a single item by its unique identifier.

delete.description: Deletes the specified item from the system.

get.description: Retrieves the containment chain of an item: the item followed by each of its parent containers. The list is ordered from the item itself (first element) outward to its root container (last element). When 'at' is supplied, the chain is reconstructed from the containment history as it was at that instant.

put.summary: Places an item inside a container
put.description: Sets the parent container of the item, recording a movement. Placing an item in the container it is already in does nothing. Requires the MoveItem permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

delete.summary: Removes an item from its container
delete.description: Clears the parent container of the item, recording a movement with no destination. An item that is not in a container is left as it is. Requires the MoveItem permission.

get.description: Retrieves a list of moviments that represents the moviment history of item.
Retrieves the per-article inventory contained in the item container. When 'at' is supplied, the inventory is reconstructed from the containment history as it was at that instant.
Retrieves a paginated list of items, including the total number of matching entries.

post.description: Creates a new item with optional partitions. Returns the generated identifier. Send an Idempotency-Key header (a GUID) to make the request safe to retry: a retry with the same key returns the first result instead of creating another item. Use a new key for a different request.

put.summary: Changes the partitions of an item
put.description: Adds and removes the partitions the an item belongs to in one request. At least one partition is required and none may be in both lists. The caller needs access to every partition it touches. Moving the item to another container is a separate operation. Requires the ChangeItemPartitions permission.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of item events, optionally filtered by article, event type, and time period, including the total number of matching entries. Requires the ReadItemEvents permission; only events whose article is accessible to the caller are returned.

post.description: Records a new item event for an event-tracked article. The eventType selects the kind: a movement of a quantity between containers, or the creation or deletion of a quantity of stock (optionally at a container). Event-based stock is not unit-tracked, so a single creation or deletion can cover many units. Returns the identifier of the recorded event. Only valid for articles whose tracking mode is Event. Send an Idempotency-Key header (a GUID) to make the request safe to retry: a retry with the same key returns the first result instead of recording the event again. Use a new key for a different request.

get.description: Retrieves a single user by its unique identifier.

put.summary: Replaces an existing user
put.description: Updates the username, names and description of a user. Use the is-active, permissions, user-groups, partitions, password and password-expiration endpoints for the rest.

delete.description: Deletes the specified user from the system.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of users, including the total number of matching entries.

post.description: Creates a new user with optional partitions, user groups, and permissions. Returns the generated identifier. Granting permissions requires ChangeUserPermissions, adding partitions or partition access requires ChangeUserPartitions, and adding user groups requires ChangeUserGroupMembers.

put.summary: Activates or deactivates a user
put.description: Sets whether the user is active. Requires the ActivateUser permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Grants and revokes permissions of a user
put.description: Adds and removes permissions in one request. At least one permission is required and none may be in both lists. The caller must hold every permission it grants or revokes. A caller cannot change its own permissions. Requires the ChangeUserPermissions permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Adds and removes the groups of a user
put.description: Adds the user to and removes it from user groups in one request. At least one group is required and none may be in both lists. Joining a group hands the user the permissions of that group and of its ancestors, so the caller must hold all of them. Requires the ChangeUserGroupMembers permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Changes the partitions of a user
put.description: Adds and removes the partitions the user belongs to (membership) and the partitions it can access in one request. At least one is required. The caller needs access to every partition it touches. Requires the ChangeUserPartitions permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Resets the password of a user
put.description: Sets a new password and requires the user to change it at the next sign-in. A caller cannot reset its own password here; use the identity password change instead. Requires the ChangeAnotherUserPassword permission.

put.summary: Sets how long the passwords of a user last
put.description: Sets the default period after which the password of the user expires. It applies the next time the password is changed; zero means it must be changed immediately. Requires the ChangeAnotherUserPassword permission.

delete.summary: Removes the password expiration of a user
delete.description: Clears the default password expiration period, so the passwords of the user no longer expire by default. Requires the ChangeAnotherUserPassword permission.

get.description: Retrieves a single user group by its unique identifier.

put.summary: Replaces an existing user group
put.description: Updates the name and description of a user group. Use the is-active, permissions, partitions and parent endpoints for the rest.

delete.description: Deletes the specified user group from the system.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of user groups, including the total number of matching entries.

post.description: Creates a new user group with optional partitions and permissions. Returns the generated identifier. Granting permissions requires ChangeUserGroupPermissions, adding partitions or partition access requires ChangeUserGroupPartitions, and setting a parent requires ChangeUserGroupParent.

put.summary: Activates or deactivates a user group
put.description: Sets whether the user group is active. Requires the ActivateUserGroup permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Grants and revokes permissions of a user group
put.description: Adds and removes permissions in one request. At least one permission is required and none may be in both lists. The caller must hold every permission it grants or revokes. Requires the ChangeUserGroupPermissions permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Changes the partitions of a user group
put.description: Adds and removes the partitions the group belongs to (membership) and the partitions it can access in one request. At least one is required. The caller needs access to every partition it touches. Requires the ChangeUserGroupPartitions permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Places a user group under a parent
put.description: Sets the parent of the group. Members of the group inherit the permissions of the parent and of its ancestors, so the caller must hold all of them. Rejects an assignment that would create a cycle. Setting the parent the group already has does nothing. Requires the ChangeUserGroupParent permission.

delete.summary: Removes the parent of a user group
delete.description: Detaches the group from its parent, so its members stop inheriting the permissions of the parent. A group without a parent is left as it is. Requires the ChangeUserGroupParent permission.

get.description: Retrieves a single partition by its unique identifier.

patch.description: Updates the name and description of a partition. Use the parent endpoint to move it.

delete.description: Deletes the specified partition from the system.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of partitions, including the total number of matching entries.

post.description: Creates a new partition under an parent. Returns the generated identifier.

put.summary: Moves a partition under another parent
put.description: Sets the parent of the partition, which changes who can access it. Rejects a move that would create a cycle. A partition always has a parent, so there is no way to clear it. Setting the parent the partition already has does nothing. Requires the ChangePartitionParent permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

post.description: Validates user credentials and returns an access token and refresh token.
Invalidates the current refresh token or session.
Uses a valid refresh token to generate a new access token.

put.summary: Changes the password of the authenticated user
put.description: Validates the current password and updates it with the new password.

post.description: Validates service-account client credentials (client id + secret) and returns a short-lived access token. Services re-exchange their credentials for a new token when the current one nears expiry; no refresh token is issued.

get.description: Retrieves a single audit log by its unique identifier, including its metadata.
Retrieves a paginated list of audit logs, including the total number of matching entries.
Gets the entity types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the audit log types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the action (permission) types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the actor types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the article types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the article tracking modes as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the barcode formats as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the item event types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the supply order statuses as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Gets the error types as id and name pairs. The id is the numeric code the API accepts and returns; the values are fixed by the application and are not read from the database.
Retrieves a single service account by its unique identifier. Never returns the secret.

put.summary: Updates a service account
put.description: Updates the description of a service account. Use the is-active, permissions and partitions endpoints for the rest.

delete.description: Deletes the specified service account. Any tokens it holds stop validating.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of service accounts, including the total number of matching entries.

post.description: Creates a service account and returns its generated client secret EXACTLY ONCE. Store the secret securely; it cannot be retrieved later (only rotated). Granting permissions requires ChangeServiceAccountPermissions, and adding partitions or partition access requires ChangeServiceAccountPartitions.

put.summary: Activates or deactivates a service account
put.description: Sets whether the service account is active. Requires the ActivateServiceAccount permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Grants and revokes permissions of a service account
put.description: Adds and removes permissions in one request. At least one permission is required and none may be in both lists. The caller must hold every permission it grants or revokes. A caller cannot change its own permissions. Requires the ChangeServiceAccountPermissions permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

put.summary: Changes the partitions of a service account
put.description: Adds and removes the partitions the account belongs to (membership) and the partitions it can access in one request. At least one is required. The caller needs access to every partition it touches. Requires the ChangeServiceAccountPartitions permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

post.description: Generates a new client secret (returned EXACTLY ONCE) and invalidates all tokens previously issued to the account. Requires the RotateServiceAccountSecret permission, which is separate from the edit permission.

get.description: Retrieves a single supply order, including its lines and receiving container, by its unique identifier.
Retrieves a paginated list of supply orders, optionally filtered by status and a case-insensitive search over the reference and description.

post.description: Creates a new draft supply order with optional lines, receiving container, and partitions. Returns the generated identifier.

post.summary: Adds a line to a draft supply order
post.description: Adds a line for the given article and ordered quantity. Only valid while the order is a draft.

patch.summary: Changes a draft supply order line quantity
patch.description: Changes the ordered quantity of a line. Only valid while the order is a draft.

delete.summary: Removes a line from a draft supply order
delete.description: Removes the line for the given article. Only valid while the order is a draft.

put.summary: Sets the receiving container of a draft supply order
put.description: Sets or clears the container into which goods are received. A null container receives goods at the root. Only valid while the order is a draft.

post.description: Commits a draft supply order, freezing its lines. Requires at least one line.

post.summary: Receives goods against a supply order
post.description: Receives the given quantities, effecting the stock change into the order's receiving container (or at the root when it has none) and advancing the order's received quantities and status. Over-receipt is permitted, and a received order accepts further receipts, so a retried request would be counted again. Send an Idempotency-Key header (a GUID) to make the request safe to retry: a retry with the same key does nothing and returns the first result. Use a new key for a different receipt.
Cancels the supply order. Not allowed once the order is received, closed, or already cancelled.
Finalizes the supply order. Allowed once at least some goods have been received.

ActiveStateDto.description: Request body of the dedicated activate/deactivate endpoints.

removeEan13.description: Clears the barcode instead of changing it.

maxQuantity.description: `null` means no cap. Only allowed for an entity-tracked allowed article.

allowedArticles.description: Empty or `null` means the container has no allow-list constraint.

ArticleDimensionUpdateDto.description:
For each axis, `null` leaves the length unchanged and the matching
`Remove*` flag clears it. The flag takes precedence over the new length.

kitComponents.description: `null` unless the article is a kit.

totalCount.description:
Whole number for entity-tracked articles; for event-tracked articles the net of movement
events (received minus dispatched), which may be fractional.

ArticleTrackingMode.description:
How the stock of an Article is tracked; chosen per article and fixed for its
lifetime.

ArticleUpdateDto.description:
`null` leaves a value unchanged. The `Remove*` flags clear the value and take
        precedence over the matching new value.

AuditLogType.description: Coarse family of a command; the exact command is in string AuditLog.CommandName.

Description.description: A free text of at most int Description.MaxLength characters; unlike Name, it may be empty.

totalCount.description:
Whole number for entity-tracked articles; for event-tracked articles the net of movement
events (received minus dispatched), which may be fractional.

fromItemContainerGuid.description: `null` for a receipt from outside any container.

toItemContainerGuid.description: `null` for a dispatch to outside any container.

occuredAt.description: UTC. `null` makes the server record the current instant.

itemGuid.description: `null` for an event-tracked article. For an item, it stays after the item is deleted.

fromItemContainerGuid.description:
`null` when there was no origin container or it has since been deleted; see
        FromNoContainer.

toItemContainerGuid.description:
`null` when there was no destination container or it has since been deleted; see
        ToNoContainer.

Name.description: A name that is not blank and has between int Name.MinLength and int Name.MaxLength characters.

Nameid.description:
A case-insensitive identifier of 3 to 100 characters, stored in lower case. It may contain only
letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', must start and end with a letter or digit, and cannot
contain consecutive special characters.

totalCount.description: Matches across all pages, ignoring pagination.
Matches across all pages, ignoring pagination.

PartitionMembershipsChangeDto.description:
Request body of the dedicated partition endpoints of articles and items, which belong to partitions
but have no partition access of their own. At least one partition must be given, and none may be in
both lists.

PartitionsChangeDto.description:
Request body of the dedicated partition endpoints. Membership is the partitions the target
belongs to; access is the partitions it may reach. At least one list must be given, and no
partition may be in both the add and the remove list of the same kind.

Password.description:
A plaintext password: 9 to 512 characters, no spaces, with at least one letter, one digit and
one special (non-letter, non-digit) character.

PasswordExpirationDto.description:
How long a user's password stays valid by default. The period is not named after the password so
the audit log does not redact it.

PermissionsChangeDto.description:
Request body of the dedicated permission endpoints: the permissions to grant and to revoke in
one request. At least one must be given, and no permission may appear in both.

ServiceAccountCreatedDto.description:
Result of creating a service account or rotating its secret. The plaintext
string ServiceAccountCreatedDto.ClientSecret is returned exactly once and cannot be retrieved again.

partitionsToAdd.description: Partitions the account belongs to. Distinct from PartitionAccessesToAdd.

ServiceTokenResultDto.description:
Unlike a user login, no refresh token is returned: the service re-exchanges its client
credentials when the access token nears expiry.

receivingContainerGuid.description:
`null` receives goods at the root. Otherwise it must be a container accessible to
        the caller.

isFullyReceived.description: Also true when more than the ordered quantity was received.

isOverReceived.description: More than the ordered quantity was received.

SupplyOrderReceiveDto.description: Goods are placed into the order's receiving container, or at the root when it has none.

articleGuid.description: Must be a line on the order.

SupplyOrderStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a SupplyOrder: Draft, then Placed, then PartiallyReceived or Received,
then Closed. An order can be Cancelled until it is received or closed.

Token.description:
An opaque security token (such as an access or refresh token): 50 to 4096 characters with no
whitespace. The domain does not interpret its value.

UserGroupsChangeDto.description:
Request body of the dedicated user-group membership endpoint. At least one group must be given,
and none may be in both lists.
